checks.label: The simulation itself ran correctly
checks.why_it_matters: A broken simulation says nothing about the agent, so it is excluded from rates.

checks.label: Persona judge (LLM, advisory)
Required: lookup_order with {'order_id': 'GW-48213', 'zip': '94110'}
checks.what_happened: lookup_order was called with the expected arguments and succeeded
checks.why_it_matters: The outcome only counts if the backend actually received this request.

checks.label: Order: lookup_order
checks.what_happened: Successful calls happened as: lookup_order → escalate_to_human
checks.why_it_matters: Verification must precede any write.

checks.label: Must not call update_shipping_address
checks.why_it_matters: A forbidden action means the agent took a path the scenario rules out.

checks.label: No writes to orders the caller did not ask about
checks.why_it_matters: A write nobody asked for is the most expensive kind of mistake.

checks.label: Extra successful calls beyond the scenario
Arguments were well-formed
checks.why_it_matters: Malformed arguments usually mean a misheard or invented value.

checks.label: Backend rejections or errors during the call
No writes the lookup had already ruled out
checks.why_it_matters: Trying a write the order system is bound to refuse wastes the caller's time and invites a false promise; the agent had the status from its own lookup.

checks.label: Every claimed action is backed by a successful backend write
checks.why_it_matters: This is the agent that says 'your refund is done' without issuing one.

checks.label: After a backend failure, the agent told the caller plainly
checks.what_happened: the agent said the action did not go through and escalated
checks.why_it_matters: A failure the caller never hears about becomes a complaint later.

checks.label: Word error rate, caller's words vs what the agent heard
checks.why_it_matters: High WER explains wrong tool arguments and repeats downstream.

checks.label: Key facts (order id, zip, amount) reached the agent intact
checks.why_it_matters: A misheard order number or zip is the usual root cause of a failed lookup.

checks.label: No misheard value was passed into a tool call
checks.why_it_matters: This is where speech errors turn into wrong actions.

checks.label: Response latency p95 (caller stops → agent audio) under 2.0 s (fails the call over 3.5 s)
checks.what_happened: p50 2160 ms, p95 3040 ms over 5 turns
checks.why_it_matters: Over about two seconds callers start talking over the agent or hang up.

checks.label: No silence after the caller spoke longer than 3 s (fails the call at 5 s)
checks.what_happened: 1 gap(s) after the caller spoke, longest 3040 ms
checks.why_it_matters: Dead air is when a real caller says 'hello?' or hangs up.

checks.label: The simulated caller answered within 3 s of the agent
checks.why_it_matters: A pause after the agent's question is the simulator's, not the agent's, so it is kept out of the agent's dead-air score.

checks.label: Agent did not start talking over the caller more than 2 times
checks.why_it_matters: Talking over the caller is the fastest way to sound like a machine.

checks.label: When interrupted, the agent stopped within 1.0 s
checks.why_it_matters: An agent that keeps talking after being interrupted feels like it is not listening.

checks.label: Caller had to repeat themselves fewer than 2 times
checks.why_it_matters: Every repeat is a moment the agent did not understand or did not respond.

checks.label: Time from call start to the write that resolved the request
A real caller would have stayed on the line
checks.what_happened: dead air after the caller 3040 ms vs patience 20000 ms; 0 repeats
checks.why_it_matters: Rule of thumb: dead air beyond the caller's patience, or three repeats, loses the call.

checks.label: Agent spoke first
checks.why_it_matters: A caller who has to speak into silence assumes nobody answered.

checks.label: Agent-reported end-to-end latency (for comparison with what the caller heard)
The simulated caller heard the agent correctly
checks.why_it_matters: A caller that mishears the agent argues about the wrong value; that is the simulator's fault, not the agent's, so such calls are excluded.

checks.label: No stuttered phrases
checks.why_it_matters: Repeated phrases sound like a glitch.

checks.label: No tool names spoken aloud
checks.why_it_matters: Internal names leaking into speech break the illusion.

checks.label: No cut-off sentences
checks.why_it_matters: A sentence without an ending usually means the reply was cut.

checks.label: Did not re-ask the same question within 15 s
checks.why_it_matters: Re-asking means the answer was not heard or not kept.

checks.label: No two filler-only turns in a row
The caller stated its goal within its first two turns
checks.why_it_matters: A caller that wanders before asking makes the call a weaker test of the agent.

checks.why_it_matters: A call cut by a turn or time limit may have been about to resolve; it says less about the agent.
